sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are uniform on the three focus tracks (`exit_confirm_screens=2`, `reentry_cooldown_screens=1`, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp=10.0` per `churn_health.tracks`), and the last 7-day operational window is clean: every focus track shows `duplicate_day_skip=false`, empty `exit_streak`, `buffered_holdings=0`, and zero adjacent flips on rules, ai_judgment, and momentum_grace (`adjacent_flip_count=0`). Lifetime decision-review cost drag remains elevated on the control and primary books (`rules` 0.4039 / 66 trades; `ai_judgment` 0.3387 / 48 trades) with watch alerts, while epoch-scoped drag is lower on primary than control (`learning_track_epoch_datum`: ai_judgment epoch `cost_drag` implied via `learning_tracks_review.reviews.ai_judgment.metrics.epoch.cost_drag` 0.1325 vs rules 0.2423). The 7-day buffered-hold replay still favours keeping two exit-confirm screens on ai_judgment (`trade_count_delta_lower_minus_higher=1`, `cost_drag_delta_lower_minus_higher=0.0024`; rules delta 0 trades / +0.0012 cost drag). The single biggest operational learning gap is that exit-shadow cohorts have `closed_count=0` on all tracks in the payload (`exit_shadow`), so post-exit grace vs rotation learning cannot yet validate whether guards are improving outcomes versus merely suppressing same-day noise.
